finding.claim: Missing authorization on /invoice/<inv_id> lets any caller read any invoice (IDOR / broken access control).
finding.source: Unauthenticated HTTP GET to /invoice/<inv_id>; attacker needs a valid invoice ID (enumerable if IDs are sequential or guessable).
finding.sink: jsonify(inv) at invoices.py:10 returns the full invoice record to the caller.

trace.note: Route registered with no auth decorator.
INVOICES.get(inv_id) lookup; only guard is 404 when missing.
Record returned without checking the caller owns it.

finding.guards_checked: No authentication in this file and no before_request hook enforcing it. No ownership check (contrast /my/invoice at invoices.py:14-17, which enforces ownership, suggesting this is a leftover unscoped route). Risk depends on whether other code adds global auth middleware; none is in this directory.

verdict.guard_found: none. invoices.py:7 has no auth decorator, and the file has no before_request hook or other auth check. The only check is `INVOICES.get(inv_id) or abort(404)` at invoices.py:9, which only handles a missing record. jsonify(inv) at invoices.py:10 returns the record with no ownership check. The only other file in the directory is the .claude skills docs, so there is no app middleware here that could add auth.
verdict.reason: The route at invoices.py:7-10 returns any invoice to an anonymous caller with no authentication or ownership check, while the sibling /my/invoice route at invoices.py:16-17 does enforce ownership, so the unscoped route is an IDOR; the attacker only needs a valid invoice ID. The one caveat is that global auth middleware could exist outside this directory, which I could not rule out.

finding.claim: Ownership checks read g.user without verifying it is set, so unauthenticated requests crash (500, possible traceback leak) or could fail open if a default user with id None is set elsewhere.
finding.source: Request with no credentials to /my/invoice/<inv_id> (line 13-14) or /my/invoices (line 21-22).
finding.sink: Ownership comparisons inv["customer"] != g.user["id"] (invoices.py:16) and i["customer"] == g.user["id"] (invoices.py:23).

trace.note: Reads g.user["id"]; AttributeError if g.user unset, TypeError if None.
Same unguarded g.user["id"] read in /my/invoices handler.

finding.guards_checked: 404 on mismatch (invoices.py:17) is correct and the type comparison fails closed for mismatched types. Nothing in this file requires or validates an authenticated user. Exploitation depends on code outside this directory that sets g.user.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only guards are abort(404) at invoices.py:15 and :17, which don't check g.user. Nothing in the directory (only invoices.py) sets g.user, authenticates the request, or wraps these routes in a before_request. The fail-open half of the claim has no support in this code.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: invoices.py:16 and :23 read g.user["id"] with no check that g.user is set, and no control in the available code prevents an anonymous request from reaching them, so it crashes with a 500. The fail-open variant is unsupported, since nothing here sets g.user to a None-id default, and the impact is an unhandled error on a single request rather than an authorization bypass.
